summary: BBN's host status report for December 6 to 18, 1971, with excluded hosts and a table of daily test results. It was replaced by RFC 288.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 287 reports ARPANET host status from December 6 to December 18, 1971, and explains why some hosts were excluded from testing. It was later replaced by RFC 288.

questions: what did the host status codes mean
why were some hosts excluded from rfc 287 tests
subtitle: A December 1971 report of ARPANET host tests and excluded hosts

tldr.problem: Network users needed information about host accessibility and the machines available as servers.
tldr.mechanism: The report lists hosts excluded from daily testing and publishes daily test results and operator-reported status or predictions.
tldr.outcome: RFC 287 was later replaced by RFC 288.

sections.title: Reporting Period and Exclusions
sections.content:
The report covers most Network Hosts from December 6 through December 18. The BBN prototype Terminal IMP was unavailable for much of the preceding period, from November 22 to December 6, because of hardware debugging; the report says there was no host status report then.

Hosts excluded from daily tests fall into two groups: those not expected to operate regularly as servers for at least two weeks, and hosts intended only as users. The Network Control Center computer is also listed as used solely for gathering network statistics.
sections.plainLanguage: BBN reports on the listed period and explains why no report covered the prior interval. Some hosts were omitted because they were not expected to serve other sites or were user-only systems.

sections.title: Daily Status Codes
sections.content:
The daily tables show a result for each host on each listed test day. D means dead or inaccessible from the BBN Terminal IMP; H means a connection opened but immediately closed or stopped responding; O means the host opened a connection and was accessible to users.

R means the destination returned a close to the initial request. T means the destination did not complete the Initial Connection Protocol and open a connection within 60 seconds. Marks identify sites that warned they might not be available at those times.
sections.plainLanguage: The report uses letters to describe each test. One code means a host was accessible; the others show different kinds of failure or partial response.

sections.title: Host Predictions and Replacement
sections.content:
A separate table gives host status or predictions supplied by operators, including labels such as Server, User only and Soon. It names the person who supplied each entry.

The unit metadata records RFC 288 as the document that later obsoleted RFC 287.
sections.plainLanguage: Operators also reported whether a host was a server, a user-only system, or expected to become a server. RFC 288 later replaced this report.
